key_insight: The paper introduces Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering (E-VQA), which asks video models to provide not just an answer, but also precise visual evidence from the video. This makes video QA more transparent and verifiable than standard black-box outputs.
problem_solved: Video LLMs can answer questions well, but their predictions are often not grounded in identifiable visual evidence. Existing explanations like text rationales or sparse boxes are too limited to capture complex video phenomena such as occlusion, motion, and non-rigid deformation.
method: Defines a new E-VQA task that jointly predicts a semantic answer and supporting evidence in the video.
Encourages fine-grained grounding so the model can point to exact visual regions or segments relevant to the answer.
Targets hard video understanding cases where evidence must track dynamic objects and changing appearances over time.
impact: This makes video AI more trustworthy, debuggable, and useful in real applications where users need to verify why a model gave an answer. For practitioners, it provides a path toward models that are not only accurate, but also interpretable and auditable.
